title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops & Top Issues
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

Purpose: This page describes our standardized approach to creating and maintaining developer experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the catalogue of top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to keep consumable, up-to-date content that accelerates developer onboarding and reduces first-line support load.

Scope
- Doc types covered: SDK guides, quickstarts, code snippets/API examples, docs-site authoring & publishing procedures, support canonical fixes.
- Audience: Developer-experience engineers, SDK maintainers, technical writers, solutions engineers, support L2.
- Exclusions: Internal meeting notes, personal notes, and ephemeral research drafts (store in Google Drive).

Ownership & SLAs
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (team channel: #devex-docs).
- Doc owner: each page must list a single owner (person) and an owning component (service or SDK). Example owner metadata is required at top of page.
- SLOs: docs-site availability >= 99.95% (monthly); critical quickstarts (top 10) must have an accuracy review every 60 days; all pages older than 90 days are flagged for review in the docs backlog.

Standards for Content (applies to all doc types)
- Tone: polished, concise, second-person ("you"), actionable.
- Structure: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step instructions (numbered), expected outcome, troubleshooting section, and links to related pages.
- Examples: include copy-paste-ready code blocks, minimal reproducer, and a short explanation of what the example does and why.
- Metadata: every page must include title, short description (1-2 sentences), owner, owner_team, created_at, last_updated, status, labels, and related_pages.

Docs-Site Operating Procedures
1) Authoring workflow
   - Create a draft in the docs repo branch named docs/{ticket-number}/{short-title}.
   - Add the following front-matter at top of the page (example):

     ---
     title: "Example Quickstart: SDK X — Uploading Files"
     owner: "alex.ramirez@redwood.ai"
     owner_team: "engineering"
     status: "draft"
     labels: ["quickstart","sdk","onboarding"]
     ---

   - Submit a PR to docs/main. Include a short description and link to a validator ticket if the page contains API or CLI changes. PR reviewers: 1 Tech Author + 1 SDK Owner.

2) Publishing checklist (required before merging to main)
   - Verify code snippets run end-to-end in the docs CI (see docs-ci pipeline).
   - Add automated snippet tests where applicable (pytest / node test harness).
   - Confirm SLO and cost notes are present for examples that generate production traffic.
   - Add labels and related_pages.
   - Run the spellcheck + accessibility audit (docs-ci step).

3) Release cadence
   - Minor doc-only changes: merged to main and deploy within 10 minutes.
   - Major API/SDK changes: coordinate with SDK release (see release-notes process) and schedule a docs deploy aligned with the SDK release window.

4) Staleness & review process
   - Every 30 days, the doc automation job audits pages modified in the last 90 days and creates review tickets for pages that reference deprecated APIs or failed snippet tests.
   - Owners must close or triage review tickets within 14 days.

SDK Guides: format & minimum content
- Purpose statement (one paragraph).
- Prerequisites: language runtime, SDK version, API key, environment variables, permissions.
- Installation: package manager command and pinned version example.
- Quickstart (5-10 minute runnable example) with code block and expected output.
- Advanced section: batching, error handling, retry/backoff recommendations, and best-practices for production (rate limiting, connection pooling).
- Migration notes for breaking changes (if applicable).
- Compatibility table (example):

  Language | SDK package | Supported runtime | Min SDK version
  --- | --- | --- | ---
  python | redwood-sdk | python 3.9+ | 1.4.0
  node   | @redwood/sdk  | node 16+       | 2.0.1

Quickstarts & Templates
- Keep quickstarts focused: 5-7 steps, 1 primary goal (e.g., basic text generation, embeddings, or local dev server).
- Provide both minimal "copy-and-run" and an expanded example showing production considerations (auth, credentials management, sample CI job).
- Templates: include a repo scaffold (GitHub template) with README, sample tests, CI config (docs-ci friendly), and license. Templates must include a small README.md that references the corresponding confluence quickstart.

API Examples (best practices)
- Use real-world parameters but redact customer data.
- Include synchronous and streaming examples where applicable.
- Provide examples for common patterns: retry on transient 5xx, exponential backoff pseudocode, and idempotency keys for request deduplication. Example pseudocode for backoff:

  retry_count = 0
  while retry_count < 5:
      try:
          call_api()
          break
      except TransientError:
          sleep(2 ** retry_count)
          retry_count += 1

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current top-10)
1) Authentication failures (invalid API key / missing header)
   - Canonical fix: ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in env and the header "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" is included. Use `redwood whoami` in CLI to validate.
2) SDK snippet tests failing due to pinned dependency mismatch
   - Canonical fix: pin matching SDK runtime in quickstart front-matter and update github actions to use the pinned matrix.
3) Streaming payload truncated / premature EOF
   - Canonical fix: verify the streaming client handles chunked transfer and doesn't close the connection on non-terminal frames; increase client-side read timeout to 60s.
4) High latency on embeddings route in region X
   - Canonical fix: route requests to regional model variant (policy: latency-first) or use the dedicated endpoint (dedicated-embeddings.redwood.internal).
5) 429 rate limit errors during load tests
   - Canonical fix: add client-side adaptive rate limiter with jitter; coordinate load-test window with platform team and request temporary soft-limits.
6) Confusing examples using deprecated parameter names
   - Canonical fix: update example and add backward-compat note; schedule a redirect from the old page to the updated quickstart.
7) Example producing nondeterministic outputs in tests
   - Canonical fix: set seed for deterministic generation in test harness and mark the example as nondeterministic in docs.
8) TLS/certificate errors on private deployments
   - Canonical fix: validate chain using openssl s_client; confirm custom CA is configured in customer kube secret and that KMS-integrations are active.
9) Incorrect billing estimate in example cost calculator
   - Canonical fix: update price-per-token and add a note with calculation steps and last_updated date.
10) Missing troubleshooting section in top quickstarts
   - Canonical fix: add a "Troubleshooting" subsection with the top 3 fail states and remediation steps.

Triage & Escalation Playbook for Doc-Related Incidents
1) L1 (support) identifies doc-related incident (broken snippet, bad parameter) and files a doc-bug ticket with severity label.
2) DevEx team triages within 4 hours for Sev=high, 48 hours for Sev=low.
3) If the issue is an API/SDK bug: escalate to SDK team and attach failing snippet/test logs.
4) For security-sensitive content: mark page confidentiality=restricted and notify security@redwood.ai immediately.

Automation & Tests
- docs-ci runs the following gates on PRs: snippet linting, snippet execution in language matrix, markdown lint, accessibility audit, and link checker.
- Snippet execution must use ephemeral API keys with read-only scopes and dedicated test projects.

Publishing templates & resources (links)
- Docs authoring template: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/docs-authoring-template
- Quickstart repo template: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-quickstart-template (use branch docs-template)
- Snippet test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-ci-snippet-runner

Appendix: Example API snippets
- Python (synchronous generation)

  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-2b", prompt="Say hello")
  print(resp.text)

- Node (streaming example)

  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const stream = client.stream.generate({ model: 'redwood-2b', prompt: 'Hello' });
  for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk); }

Maintenance notes
- Annual cleanup: retire templates that have no traffic for >12 months and no active owners.
- Budget note: doc automation infra budget is tracked under eng-platform/observability with a monthly cap of $500.

Contact & escalation
- Primary contact: #devex-docs (Slack) and devex-docs@redwood.ai (email).
- Oncall rotation: see /confluence/eng-developer-experience/runbooks/doc-oncall-rotation.
